issues.body: The selector remains `started && /^[[:space:]]*path:[[:space:]]*target[[:space:]]*$/`, so it ignores `path: "target"` and `path: 'target'` even though YAML resolves both to the same checkout destination. A pinned unquoted decoy can be counted as the sole target checkout while the real model checkout uses a quoted target path and a moving or omitted ref. The extractor then returns the decoy's expected ref rather than `<ambiguous>`, leaving the marquee assertions green on an unbound model tree. This is materially the same trust-binding bypass reported in round 4, and none of the added mutants covers quoted scalar equivalence.
issues.fix_hint: Parse the YAML value or normalize supported quoted and unquoted scalar spellings before comparing the destination, then fail closed unless exactly one checkout step semantically resolves to `target`. Add mutants with a correctly pinned unquoted decoy plus a real checkout using each of `path: "target"` and `path: 'target'` with a moving or absent ref; both must produce `<ambiguous>` or otherwise refuse.
issues.title: Quoted target paths still bypass checkout uniqueness

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 major finding remains unresolved. `_model_target_checkout_ref` still recognizes only the raw unquoted spelling `path: target`; YAML-equivalent quoted scalars remain invisible. A pinned unquoted decoy can therefore be counted as the unique target checkout while the actual model checkout uses `path: "target"` or `path: 'target'` with a moving or absent ref. The extensive new mutants do not exercise either quoted spelling, so the trust-binding claim remains bypassable. Progress is stagnant.
